note: Order every 2 days (even days), each order covering 2 days of forecast ×1.1 for both products; the risk is that the open-loop plan can't absorb runs of high demand, so shortages pile up.
Order every 3 days at the bare forecast, trimmed to fit the 280 cap; it saves on the 40 fee, but holding costs rise and shortages are frequent with no safety stock.
Order daily at forecast ×1.1 with minimal stock; the risk is the ~1100 in order fees, which eats the holding savings.
2-day cycle with ×1.2 safety (a shortage costs about 10–11, a leftover usually carries over cheaply); the risk is stock accumulating and spoiling for product 0.
2-day cycle at the bare forecast; it's cheap on spoilage, but the mean multiplier of 1.046 means a systematic shortfall and penalties.
2-day cycle with separate safety factors: product 0 ×1.15, and product 1 ×1.25 (8-day shelf life, higher shortage cost); the risk is excess product 1 piling up and holding costs at 0.5.
Large batches every 4 days (minimal fees); the risk is high holding costs, near-cap peaks of 280 that lose deliveries, and product 0 spoiling.
Aggressive 2-day cycle at ×1.35 to almost never run short; the risk is systematic overstock: spoilage, holding, and hitting the cap around day 9.
